`@mysten/sui` 3.0 removes the JSON-RPC transport. If you still use `SuiJsonRpcClient`, move to
[`SuiGrpcClient`](/sui/clients/grpc) (recommended) or [`SuiGraphQLClient`](/sui/clients/graphql) by
following [Migrating from JSON-RPC](/sui/migrations/sui-2.0/json-rpc-migration), which maps every
JSON-RPC method to its replacement. Code that already runs on gRPC or GraphQL needs few or no
changes.

Every `@mysten/*` package with a peer dependency on `@mysten/sui`, except the legacy
`@mysten/dapp-kit`, gets a new release that requires `@mysten/sui@^3`: a major release, or a minor
release for packages still on 0.x. `@mysten/dapp-kit-react` also gets a major release, because it
depends on `@mysten/dapp-kit-core` 2.0. Apart from the items below, these releases have no breaking
changes: upgrade them together with `@mysten/sui`.

The legacy `@mysten/dapp-kit` has a peer dependency on `@mysten/sui` and uses JSON-RPC, so it can't
run on 3.0 or keep a 2.x copy of its own.
[Migrate to `@mysten/dapp-kit-react`](/sui/migrations/sui-2.0/dapp-kit) before upgrading.

## Breaking changes

### Removed JSON-RPC APIs

- **`@mysten/sui/jsonRpc` no longer supports JSON-RPC.** Code that imports it still loads, but
  `SuiJsonRpcClient`, `JsonRpcHTTPTransport` and the JSON-RPC error classes throw when constructed,
  and `isSuiJsonRpcClient` returns `false`. Its types, such as `ObjectOwner`, are deprecated aliases
  of `any`. Follow [Migrating from JSON-RPC](/sui/migrations/sui-2.0/json-rpc-migration), and use
  the `SuiClientTypes` equivalents from `@mysten/sui/client` for the types.
- **`getJsonRpcFullnodeUrl` throws.** Pass the full node URL (for example
  `https://fullnode.mainnet.sui.io:443`) to `SuiGrpcClient`'s `baseUrl`.
- **`normalizedTypeToMoveTypeSignature` is removed.** `getMoveFunction` already returns
  `OpenSignature`s.
- **Untyped pure values are no longer supported.** `SuiJsonRpcClient` serialized `UnresolvedPure`
  inputs, such as raw Move call arguments in v1 transaction JSON restored with `Transaction.from`,
  from the Move function signature; `SuiGrpcClient` and `SuiGraphQLClient` reject them. Pass typed
  values such as `tx.pure.u64(...)` instead.

### Core API

- **`listDynamicFields` pagination loops may need a type annotation.** If a loop that passes the
  cursor back in fails with `TS7022`, annotate the page as
  `SuiClientTypes.ListDynamicFieldsResponse`.
- **On `SuiGrpcClient`, `listDynamicFields` with `include: { value: true }` returns a dynamic object
  field's child object as its value**, matching `SuiGraphQLClient`: `value.bcs` is the child
  object's BCS contents instead of its ID. Read the child's ID from `childId`.
- **On `SuiGraphQLClient`, an empty last page of `listTransactions` or `listEvents` has `null`
  cursors**, as on `SuiGrpcClient`. When polling, keep your previous cursor
  (`cursor = page.endCursor ?? cursor`).
- **On `SuiGraphQLClient`, a transaction's `events` take `packageId` and `module` from the Move call
  that emitted the event**, as `listEvents` and `SuiGrpcClient` do, rather than from the event type.

### Transaction data and BCS

- **Transaction data (`include: { transaction: true }`) has a `kind`.** Inputs and commands carry
  `$kind`, so narrow with `input.$kind === 'Pure'` rather than `'Pure' in input`. Decode transaction
  bytes into this type with `parseTransactionDataBcs`. See
  [transaction data](/sui/clients/executing#transaction-data). It is no longer the builder's
  serialized type, so to rebuild a `Transaction` from a query result, request
  `include: { bcs: true }` and pass the result's `bcs` to `Transaction.from`.
- **`bcs.Owner` has a `Party` variant, and `bcs.MoveObjectType`'s `AccumulatorBalanceWrapper` is
  renamed to `SuiBalanceAccumulatorField`.**
- **System transaction kinds decoded with `bcs.TransactionKind` use named fields instead of
  tuples**, and `authenticatorObjInitialSharedVersion` and `randomnessObjInitialSharedVersion` are
  renamed to `authenticatorObjectInitialSharedVersion` and `randomnessObjectInitialSharedVersion`.
- **`SuiClientTypes.MoveLocation.function` (the function index) is removed.** Use
  `location.functionName`.
- **`bcs.TransactionEffects` tuples are structs with named fields**, for example `changedObjects`
  entries (`{ objectId, inputState, outputState, idOperation }`), `IntegerTuple`
  (`{ first, second }`) and V1 `modifiedAtVersions` entries (`{ objectId, version }`).
  `InsufficientBalanceForWithdraw` is renamed to `InsufficientFundsForWithdraw` and
  `congested_objects` to `congestedObjects`. The encoded bytes are unchanged.
- **Multisig BCS fields are camelCase:** `multisigPk` instead of `multisig_pk` and `pkMap` instead
  of `pk_map`. The old names still work on `parseSerializedSignature` results but are deprecated.
- **Execution error names in `effects.status` match `SuiGrpcClient` everywhere**, including
  `SuiGraphQLClient` and dApp Kit wallet results: `InvalidBcsBytes`, `InvalidUsageOfPureArgument`,
  `ConsensusObjectOperationNotAllowed` and `PackageIdDoesNotMatch` replace `InvalidBCSBytes`,
  `InvalidUsageOfPureArg`, `SharedObjectOperationNotAllowed` and `PackageIDDoesNotMatch`.
- **`parseGrpcTransactionResponse` needs `transaction.sender` in the read mask.**
- **`parseTransactionBcs` returns the transaction builder's `TransactionData`** from
  `@mysten/sui/transactions`, not `SuiClientTypes.TransactionData`. Use `parseTransactionDataBcs`
  where you need the client type.
- **Building or serializing a transaction that calls `0x2::address_alias` throws.** Pass
  `restrictedMoveCalls: []` to the client constructor, or to `build` or `toJSON`, to allow it. See
  [Restricted Move calls](/sui/transactions/reference#restricted-move-calls).

### Transports

- **gRPC-web uses the binary format by default.** If a proxy in front of your full node only
  supports `application/grpc-web-text`, pass `format: 'text'`.
- **Client URLs are checked at construction.** A GraphQL `url` or gRPC `baseUrl` that is neither an
  absolute http(s) URL nor a path starting with `/` throws when the client is created.
- **Network errors changed.** `SuiGrpcClient` reports `UNAVAILABLE` instead of `INTERNAL`, and
  `SuiGraphQLClient` throws `SuiGraphQLRequestError`, with the original error as `cause`, for
  network failures and malformed or unreadable bodies.
- **The raw gRPC `GetPackageRequest` type requires a `selector`.** Existing
  `client.movePackageService.getPackage({ packageId })` calls still work at runtime. To satisfy the
  type, pass `selector: { oneofKind: undefined }` or build the request with
  `GrpcTypes.GetPackageRequest.create({ packageId })`.

### Signature verification

- **`verifyPersonalMessageSignature`, `verifyTransactionSignature`,
  `isValidPersonalMessageSignature` and `isValidTransactionSignature` require a `client` or
  `offline: true`.** Without either it's a type error; at runtime they verify offline and log a
  warning. With a client, the node verifies the signature and checks zkLogin signatures; with
  `address`, it also accepts the address's [address aliases](/sui/cryptography#address-aliases), and
  throws on nodes that can't check them unless you pass `checkAddressAliases: false`. With
  `offline: true`, zkLogin signatures throw. See
  [Online or offline](/sui/cryptography#online-or-offline) for which to choose.
- **With a client, the public key the verify helpers return may belong to one of the address's
  aliases.** Use `address`, not `publicKey.toSuiAddress()`, as the account's identity.
- **`verifyZkLoginSignature` accepts signatures from the address's aliases** and throws on nodes
  that can't check address aliases. It's deprecated: use `client.core.verifySignature`.

## Other packages

- **`@mysten-incubation/sponsor`'s `userSignatureMatchesSender` verifies on the node**, and fails
  with `ANALYSIS_FAILED` if the node can't be reached.
- **`@mysten/wallet-sdk`'s `restrictedMoveCalls` and `@mysten-incubation/sponsor`'s
  `noRestrictedMoveCalls` take `{ restrictedMoveCalls }`** (`package`, `package::module` or
  `package::module::function` entries) instead of `addressAliases` and `targets`, and throw on any
  other option. The list replaces the default, so keep `'0x2::address_alias'` in it to keep flagging
  alias changes. Results no longer have a `level`, and `matchedBy` is a single entry instead of an
  array.
- **`@mysten/wallet-standard` and `@mysten/kiosk` no longer use JSON-RPC types.** Import legacy
  response types from the `SuiJsonRpcTypes` namespace in `@mysten/wallet-standard`.
  `TransferPolicy.owner` in `@mysten/kiosk` is a `SuiClientTypes.ObjectOwner`.

Wallets that still implement the deprecated `sui:signAndExecuteTransactionBlock` feature can build
its legacy response from a gRPC or GraphQL execution with `@mysten/wallet-sdk/json-rpc-compat`:

```typescript
import {
	mappableIncludeFor,
	transactionBlockResponseFromExecution,
} from '@mysten/wallet-sdk/json-rpc-compat';

// `input` is the dApp's `sui:signAndExecuteTransactionBlock` input; `bytes` (a `Uint8Array`) and
// `signature` are what the wallet signed.
const result = await client.core.executeTransaction({
	transaction: bytes,
	signatures: [signature],
	include: mappableIncludeFor(input.options),
});

return transactionBlockResponseFromExecution(result.Transaction ?? result.FailedTransaction, {
	bytes,
	signatures: [signature],
	options: input.options,
});
```

For wallet code that still reads the JSON-RPC dry-run shape, `dryRunFromSimulation` builds a
`DryRunTransactionBlockResponse` from the simulated transaction
(`result.Transaction ?? result.FailedTransaction`) of a `simulateTransaction` call made with
`include: { balanceChanges: true, effects: true, events: true, objectTypes: true, transaction: true }`.

## Dependencies that still require 2.x

You can upgrade before your dependencies release versions for 3.0. How a dependency lists
`@mysten/sui` decides which copy it uses:

- **A regular dependency on 2.x:** it installs its own 2.x copy and keeps working on it.
  `Transaction`s built by its copy skip the
  [restricted Move calls](/sui/transactions/reference#restricted-move-calls) check.
- **A peer dependency on `^2`:** npm refuses to install it next to 3.0. pnpm and Yarn print a
  warning and give it your 3.0 copy.

Run `npm ls @mysten/sui` or `pnpm why @mysten/sui` to see which copies you have.

Let packages keep their own 2.x copy where you can. Only values that cross between your code and the
package are affected:

- Clients, `Transaction`s and signers from your copy may not type-check where its API expects its
  own, and fail its `instanceof` checks on SDK classes. A package that accepts `ClientWithCoreApi`
  and doesn't use `instanceof` on SDK classes accepts them at runtime.
- A package that calls methods on your 3.0 client gets 3.0 results, with the [Core API](#core-api)
  and [transaction data](#transaction-data-and-bcs) changes above.

If a package needs to use your copy, for example a peer dependency that npm won't install, add an
override:

```json title="package.json (npm)"
{
	"overrides": {
		"@mysten/sui": "$@mysten/sui"
	}
}
```

`$@mysten/sui` reuses the version in your own `dependencies`.

```yaml title="pnpm-workspace.yaml (pnpm 10.5 and later)"
overrides:
  '@mysten/sui': '$@mysten/sui'
```

Earlier pnpm versions ignore overrides in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: put the same entry under
`pnpm.overrides` in `package.json` instead. pnpm resolves `$@mysten/sui` from the root
`package.json`, so if only a workspace package depends on `@mysten/sui`, write the range instead,
for example `^3.0.0`.

```json title="package.json (Yarn, Bun)"
{
	"resolutions": {
		"@mysten/sui": "^3.0.0"
	}
}
```

Yarn still prints a peer dependency warning, which you can ignore.

An override applies to every package, so all of them run on 3.0, as does a peer dependency that pnpm
or Yarn gives your copy. The breaking changes above affect these packages as they affect your code.
Most often, a package that imports `@mysten/sui/jsonRpc` loads, but throws when it uses JSON-RPC. It
needs a release for 3.0; until then, don't add an override, so that a regular dependency keeps its
own 2.x copy.

Test the flows that use each dependency, and remove the override once every dependency supports 3.0.

## Libraries built on `@mysten/sui`

If you publish a package that uses `@mysten/sui`, release a version for 3.0 that:

- **Lists `@mysten/sui@^3` in `peerDependencies`**, not `dependencies`, so apps keep a single copy.
  See [Building SDKs](/sui/sdk-building#use-mysten-packages-as-peer-dependencies).
- **Doesn't import `@mysten/sui/jsonRpc`.** On 3.0 its classes and `getJsonRpcFullnodeUrl` throw,
  and its types are `any`.
- **Accepts `ClientWithCoreApi`** from `@mysten/sui/client` instead of a specific client class, and
  reads through `client.core`.
- **Doesn't use `instanceof` on SDK classes**, which fails for values from another copy of
  `@mysten/sui`. Use `isTransaction` from `@mysten/sui/transactions`, `isSuiGrpcClient` from
  `@mysten/sui/grpc` and `isSuiGraphQLClient` from `@mysten/sui/graphql`.

## New in 3.0

- `listTransactions` filters accept `affectedAddress` and `affectedObject`, and `sender` combines
  with other predicates.
- `listTransactions` and `listEvents` accept `startCheckpoint` and `endCheckpoint`, and `after` and
  `before` can be combined to read a window.
- `doGasSelection` is available on every client's `simulateTransaction`.
- A `listCheckpoints` method for paging through checkpoints.
- `SuiGraphQLClient.subscribe` runs GraphQL subscriptions; `subscriptionUrl` sets their endpoint.
- Resumable checkpoint, transaction, and event streams on `SuiGrpcClient` and `SuiGraphQLClient`.
  See [Resumable ledger streams](/sui/clients/streaming).
- `client.core.listDynamicFields({ include: { value: true } })` returns each field's value with the
  listing, on every client.
- `client.core.verifySignature`, which verifies a personal message or transaction signature on the
  node and checks address aliases, and `client.core.getAddressAliases`.
